sections.title: Putting a whole order together
sections.content: Every order is built from the same pieces: who asks (the verb ending), how much (a number, *kiló* or nothing), a colour if you like, and the thing with its *-t*. Two choices decide the rest. If the thing has *a / az*, *ezt* or *azt*, use the definite verb (*kérem, kérjük, veszik*). If it has *egy*, a number, *kiló* or nothing, use the ending you already knew (*kérek, kérünk, vesznek*). With a number the noun stays singular; with nothing before it, the plural is *-kat / -ket*.

sections.title: Order and verb
rows: number + colour + noun -t: any, so kérek
a + colour + plural: the ones, so kérem

items.english: I'd like two kilos of red apples.
We'll take this one, not that one.

sections.content: When a sentence goes wrong, check the object first. The verb ending follows from it, the number follows from the subject. *Két kiló piros almát* never has a plural, and *a piros almákat* always has the definite verb.
